standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label remark-finite-presentation (proof line 2447) and Algebra, label algebra-lemma-unique-prime-over-localize-below (proof line 2452)

standard_prerequisites.name: The algebraic induction step for a flat map with geometrically integral fibres
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-induction-step, invoked at proof line 2456
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives that the first map of the devissage is universally injective over the base and that the cokernel is flat at the point, which makes the induction hypothesis applicable to the cokernel.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finiteness of presentation of an extension, freeness of a projective module over a local ring, and projectivity of the smooth pieces
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, labels algebra-lemma-extension (proof line 2465) and algebra-theorem-projective-free-over-local-ring (proof line 2471); Same chapter flat.tex, label lemma-fibres-irreducible-flat-projective-nonnoetherian (proof line 2470)
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that M_1 is finitely presented as a B_1-module once its cokernel is, that the smooth algebra B_1 is free over the local base because it is projective, and that the decomposition of the cokernel supplies the required decomposition of M_1.

core_obligations: Reduce to the first step of the devissage: let the given devissage be indexed by i, note that N is finitely presented over S exactly when M_1 is finitely presented over B_1, and that the localisation of N at the given prime is the localisation of M_1 at the corresponding prime because the two local rings agree; hence (S, N) may be replaced by (B_1, M_1) (proof lines 2442-2455).

Apply the induction step to the first map: the map from the finite free module to M_1 is universally injective over the base and its cokernel is flat at the point, and the remaining tail of the devissage is a complete devissage of that cokernel at the point, so the induction hypothesis gives that the cokernel is finitely presented over B_1, free over the base and decomposed as a direct sum of powers of smooth algebras (proof lines 2456-2463).

Read off the conclusion: from the finite presentation of the cokernel, M_1 is finitely presented over B_1 by the extension lemma; the short exact sequence exhibiting M_1 as the direct sum of the free module and the cokernel gives the required decomposition over the base; and each smooth algebra in the decomposition is free over the base because it is projective over the local base by the non Noetherian projectivity lemma (proof lines 2464-2473).
proof_roadmap: Replace the pair by the first step of the devissage (proof lines 2442-2455).
Apply the induction step and the induction hypothesis to the tail (proof lines 2456-2463).
Deduce finite presentation, the direct sum decomposition and freeness of the pieces (proof lines 2464-2473).
difficulty_reason: The lemma draws concrete consequences from the existence of a complete devissage: for a module flat at a prime over the maximal ideal of a local base, it concludes that the module is finitely presented, free over the base, and a direct sum of powers of smooth algebras (statement lines 2425-2440, tag 05I4). The proof runs an induction on the length of the devissage: it first replaces the pair by the first step using the identification of localisations, then applies the induction step to see that the first map is universally injective with flat cokernel so that the induction hypothesis applies to the tail, and finally assembles finite presentation from the extension lemma and freeness from projectivity over the local base. The induction and the assembly are the substance, so the claim is H2.
